topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic welcomes students to the final lecture and outlines the intended learning outcomes regarding cancer treatment modalities.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional treatment modalities—surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated systemic toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting cancer cell vulnerabilities and repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic strategies designed to exploit inherent tumor vulnerabilities, including hormone dependency, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene addiction and small-molecule kinase inhibitors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting oncogene-driven signaling through small-molecule kinase inhibitors, detailing their mechanisms, resistance pathways, and clinical consequences.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates selectively target cell surface antigens to eliminate tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immune surveillance and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the biological evidence for antitumor immunity and the clinical application of immunotherapies that reactivate or engineer T cells to target cancer.

topics.label: Current challenges, historical trends, and future perspectives in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader landscape of oncology by reviewing historical progress, modern therapeutic challenges, genomic stratification, and emerging ethical dilemmas.
